name: Capital One Venture X
features: 5x flights & vacation rentals via Capital One Travel
10x hotels & rental cars via Capital One Travel
practical_advice: Travel often? Venture X still works: $300 portal credit plus 10k anniversary miles beats the $395 fee. Lounges got tighter in 2026—you're free, but guests are $45 and authorized users cost $125/yr.

name: Chase Sapphire Reserve
practical_advice: Sapphire Reserve is a high-fee, high-effort lifestyle card that only makes sense if your routine naturally hits several credits offered.

name: American Express Platinum
practical_advice: $895 luxury travel card that only makes sense if you'll actually use the brand-specific credits. The Saks credit is gone as of July 2026 and Lufthansa lounge access ends October 1, 2026 — the fee math is tighter than the marketing sheet suggests.

name: Wells Fargo Active Cash®
practical_advice: A dead-simple, “set it and forget it” 2% cash-back card with a strong cell-phone protection perk if you pay your wireless bill on it.

name: Citi Double Cash® Card
practical_advice: Best for a simple $0-fee 2% card. Set it as your default for everyday spend.

name: American Express® Gold Card
practical_advice: The Gold Card makes sense if you spend real money on food and don't mind juggling credits. The May 2026 refresh kept the $325 fee, bumped prepaid Amex Travel hotels to 5x, and swapped Goldbelly and Wine.com out of the dining credit for Buffalo Wild Wings and Wonder.

name: Capital One Savor
features: 5% hotels, vacation rentals & rental cars via Capital One Travel
practical_advice: Savor shines for food-heavy budgets: 3% on groceries, dining, entertainment and streaming with a $0 annual fee, plus an easy $200 bonus after $500 in 3 months.

name: Chase Sapphire Preferred
practical_advice: Nice starter travel card: $95 fee, 3x dining and easy transfer partners; the $100 annual hotel credit alone can cover the fee if you book travel yearly.

name: Chase Freedom Unlimited®
practical_advice: Great $0-fee starter: 5x travel, 3x dining/drugstores, 1.5x elsewhere; pair with a Sapphire for better travel value.

name: Wells Fargo Autograph Journey®
practical_advice: Great mid-tier travel card—$50 annual airline credit helps offset the $95 fee if you book at least one flight a year.

name: American Express Blue Business® Plus (BBP)
features: 2x points on everything (up to $50k per year)
practical_advice: This is a great card that holds AMEX points for no annual fee and earns a great rate on non categorized spend.

name: Bilt Blue Card
features: Up to 1.25x rent & mortgage (no fee, no cap)
1x everyday + 4% Bilt Cash toward housing points
practical_advice: The $0-fee card in Bilt's 2.0 lineup. Rent and even mortgages earn with no cap, but housing points come from everyday spend—charge roughly 75% of your housing payment elsewhere to earn a full 1x. Great as a daily driver; weak if card spend is small.

name: Citi Custom Cash® Card
features: 5x top category each billing cycle (to $500; then 1x)
practical_advice: Citi stopped accepting applications on May 28, 2026. Existing cardholders keep everything—5% on your top category up to $500 each cycle, no annual fee—but the only way in now is a product change from another Citi card. If you have it, keep it.

name: Discover it® Cash Back
practical_advice: Activate 5% each quarter, cap $1,500; year-one Cashback Match doubles earnings. Now serviced by Capital One, which added standing 5% on Capital One Travel and Entertainment.

name: Delta SkyMiles® Reserve American Express Card
practical_advice: For real Delta flyers only. The 15 Sky Club visits, companion certificate, and $560 in annual credits carry the $650 — casual travelers will feel it.

name: United Club℠ Infinite
practical_advice: Fly United a lot? The lounge membership, 2 bags, Premier Access, and credits can offset $695; if you rarely use clubs, this will feel expensive.

name: Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive
practical_advice: Refreshed August 2026: $695 fee (up $100) with new $500 AA Vacations and $100 inflight credits. The built-in Admirals Club membership is still the reason to carry it—use the lounge and it covers most of the fee; otherwise you're paying more for coupons you may not use.

name: Southwest Rapid Rewards Priority Credit Card
practical_advice: Best for Southwest regulars who want the free bag plus seat selection at booking and free Extra Legroom upgrades; if you rarely fly Southwest, the $229 fee will feel heavy.

name: Amazon Prime Visa
practical_advice: If you already pay for Prime, this is easy 5% back on Amazon—no annual fee, no brain space required.

name: American Express® Classic Green Card
practical_advice: Closed to new applications since July 2026 and renamed the Classic Green Card. If you already hold it, nothing changed — $150 fee, 3x on dining, travel, and transit, and a $219 CLEAR+ credit that more than covers the fee.

name: Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express
practical_advice: Big on groceries and streaming? 6% cash back beats the $95 fee fast — and the Disney credit is now $10/month with no minimum spend, so that alone more than covers it. Watch the $6,000 grocery cap.

name: Capital One Venture Rewards
features: 5x hotels, vacation rentals & rental cars via Capital One Travel
practical_advice: Venture added a $100 annual hotel credit in 2026 that more than covers its $95 fee if you book one hotel through Capital One Travel. That makes it a genuinely easy keep, not just a stepping stone to Venture X.

name: Wells Fargo Autograph®
practical_advice: Simple $0 travel card: 3x travel & dining, no credits to juggle. Upgrade to Autograph Journey if you'll use the $50 airline credit.

name: Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards
practical_advice: An easy $0-fee keeper if you already bank with Bank of America: a 3% category you can switch monthly (6% your first year) plus automatic 2% groceries. The May 2026 BofA Rewards overhaul moved the 75% boost to $1M in balances; if you don't bank there, a flat 2% card usually beats it.

name: Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards
practical_advice: One card to swipe everywhere—1.5% on everything, and the BofA Rewards boost is what lifts it past a plain 2% card. The first-year 2% promo is gone, replaced by a bigger $250 bonus. The 3% foreign fee makes it a poor travel card.

name: U.S. Bank Smartly™ Visa Signature® Card
features: Up to 4% with $100k+ in Bank Smartly Checking (first $10k/cycle)
practical_advice: Only worth chasing if you keep real money in a Bank Smartly Checking account—savings and investment balances no longer count toward the 2.5%–4% tiers, and the bonus rate caps at the first $10,000 per cycle. Otherwise it's a plain $0-fee 2% card.

name: Fidelity® Rewards Visa Signature® Card
practical_advice: Simple 2% everywhere, no fee. Best if you redeem into a Fidelity account; otherwise it's just another flat-2% card.

name: Citi Strata Elite℠ Card
practical_advice: Limited credits and portal hoops. Outside the welcome bonus, most travelers find better value with other premium cards.

name: U.S. Bank Altitude® Go Visa Signature®
practical_advice: It's a pretty nice dining card, but there is a $2000 cap per quarter. You also need a U.S. Bank account to redeem cash back for full value.

name: Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi
practical_advice: Great Costco card if you buy gas and shop there; rewards arrive once a year as a certificate, not monthly cash.

name: Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card
practical_advice: Get it if you'll use the resort credits, flight credits, and yearly free nights; otherwise the $550 fee will sting.

name: Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® (Amex)
practical_advice: Worth it for Marriott regulars who'll use Platinum status, the 85K free night cert (now reaching 110K-point hotels), and the $25/month dining credit. If you only want a certificate, Chase's $95 Boundless is far better value.

name: World of Hyatt® Credit Card
practical_advice: An easy keeper if you use the annual Category 1–4 free night and eat out monthly. Cardmembers can now book award nights 13 months out instead of 12, which helps at the small properties that sell out instantly.

name: IHG® One Rewards Premier Credit Card
practical_advice: Book IHG at least once a year? The 40k free night plus the 4th-night-free perk can more than cover the $99 fee.

name: Citi Strata Premier
practical_advice: 3x on dining, groceries, flights + easy $100 hotel discount. Best if you'll transfer points; cash-back purists may want a simpler card.

name: Delta SkyMiles Gold American Express Card
practical_advice: Solid for casual Delta flyers: free first and second checked bags, priority boarding, 15% off awards, and $0 fee the first year. The new $120 rideshare credit doesn't start until year two.

name: Apple Card
practical_advice: Still a simple, no-fee card that pays best if you actually use Apple Pay. Chase is replacing Goldman Sachs as issuer, but nothing changes for cardholders yet. If most of your spending isn't Apple Pay, a flat 2% card earns more.

name: United Quest Card
practical_advice: Fly United yearly? The automatic $200 TravelBank, two free bags, and 4x on United carry the $350 fee—just pick one or two partner credits you'll actually use on purpose.

name: United Explorer Card
practical_advice: Fly United yearly? Free bag, two lounge passes, and $500+ in partner credits can beat the $150 fee (waived year one)—if you actually use them.

name: JetBlue Plus Card
practical_advice: Straightforward value for casual JetBlue flyers: the free checked bag plus the $100 JetBlue Vacations credit can cover the $99 fee on a single trip. Barclays periodically runs elevated offers, so check before applying.

name: Southwest Rapid Rewards Premier Card
practical_advice: Fly Southwest? 6,000 anniversary points, a free checked bag for up to 9 people, Preferred seat selection, and a 15% code beat the $149 fee with one or two trips.

name: Southwest Rapid Rewards Plus Card
practical_advice: Free first bag for you and up to 8 companions, 3k anniversary points, and a 10% code—one Southwest trip with a checked bag covers the $99.

name: Delta SkyMiles Platinum American Express Card
practical_advice: Worth it if you fly Delta a few times a year and will actually use the $390 in annual credits plus the companion certificate. No lounge access at all — that's the Reserve.

name: Atmos Rewards Summit Visa Infinite Credit Card
practical_advice: The rare airline card that earns well overseas—3x on foreign purchases and dining, not just flights. Eight lounge passes, free bags for up to six companions, and an anniversary 25K companion award stack up fast against the $395. Skip it if you don't fly Alaska or Hawaiian.

name: Atmos Rewards Ascent Visa Signature Credit Card
practical_advice: The simple choice if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian yearly: the free first bag for you and up to six companions, plus the annual $99 companion fare after $6,000 spend, beats the $95 fee on one round trip together. Want lounges and credits? Go Summit.

name: IHG One Rewards Traveler Credit Card
practical_advice: No fee, Silver status, 4th night free, and a $10 monthly Instacart credit: great if you book IHG awards. Want an annual free night? Choose Premier instead.

name: Marriott Bonvoy Boundless Credit Card
practical_advice: Easy $95 keeper if you use the 35k free night, and up to $100/yr in airline credits ($50 per half after $250 booked direct) can cover the fee on its own — existing cardmembers have to enroll.

name: Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select World Elite Mastercard
image_url: images/Citi® : AAdvantage® Platinum Select® World Elite Mastercard®.webp
practical_advice: Best for American flyers: free bag, early boarding, and a $125 flight discount after $20k; no lounge access and few frills.

name: American Airlines AAdvantage MileUp Card
practical_advice: Easy no-fee AA miles at groceries; solid starter, but foreign fees apply and there's no bag, boarding, or lounge perks.

name: Hilton Honors American Express Surpass Card
practical_advice: Great if you hit Hilton a few times yearly—the $200 credits and Gold perks can easily beat the fee.

name: Hilton Honors American Express Card
practical_advice: If you touch Hilton a couple times a year, this is the simple, no-fee way to collect points with built-in Silver status (unlocks the fifth night free on awards).

name: Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express
practical_advice: An easy keeper if your spending lives in groceries, gas, and online shopping — no annual fee and caps big enough for most households. The Home Chef credit is gone, so Disney streaming ($7/month) is the only credit left.

name: Marriott Bonvoy Bountiful® Credit Card
practical_advice: You get automatic Gold Elite status, 1,000 bonus points per stay, and solid 4x on dining and U.S. supermarkets up to $15,000 a year.

name: Marriott Bonvoy Bold® Credit Card
practical_advice: Painless no-fee way to earn Bonvoy points with automatic Silver status, and the $10 monthly Instacart credit is up to $120 a year on a card that costs nothing.

name: PayPal Cashback Mastercard®
practical_advice: If you live in PayPal—buying online, paying friends for group gifts, tapping PayPal at checkout—this is easy, automatic cash back with no annual fee.

name: Chase Freedom Flex®
practical_advice: It's the "do-a-lot-for-$0" card: rotating 5% categories, 5% travel via Chase, and 3% on dining and drugstores.

name: DoorDash Rewards Mastercard®
practical_advice: If you live on DoorDash, this is the easy pick: 4% on-app, 3% direct dining, 2% groceries, and a free year of DashPass that starts right away.

name: Venmo Credit Card
practical_advice: If your spending moves around, this is an easy $0-fee way to have 3% automatically land where you spend most each month. Rewards post to your Venmo balance.

name: Sam's Club® Mastercard®
practical_advice: Best for Plus members: 5% gas, 3% dining, and 3% in-club that stacks with the Plus 2% for up to 5% at Sam's. Membership went up $10 in May 2026 ($60 Club / $120 Plus), but the Plus Sam's Cash cap also rose to $750/year.

name: Robinhood Gold Card
practical_advice: A very strong flat-rate card if you already pay for Robinhood Gold: 3% on everything beats every 2% card, and about $1,700 of annual spend covers the $50 membership. The catch: cards opened after July 2026 pay a 3% foreign transaction fee, so it's no longer the card to take abroad.

name: Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card
features: 5% hotels and rental cars via Capital One Travel
practical_advice: Flat 1.5% back with no annual fee and a 0% intro APR for 15 months. Best if you're already in the Capital One ecosystem—otherwise a no-fee 2% card earns more.

name: Capital One VentureOne Rewards Credit Card
features: 5x hotels, vacation rentals & rental cars via Capital One Travel
practical_advice: VentureOne is the no-fee starter: 1.25x everywhere, 5x on portal travel, 0% intro APR for 15 months. No credits and no lounge access—if you'd pay $95, Venture's new $100 hotel credit makes it the better card.

name: U.S. Bank Altitude® Connect Visa Signature® Card
practical_advice: Altitude Connect is a rare no-fee travel card with real multipliers. Redemptions are simple and you get a small taste of premium perks without paying a premium fee.

name: U.S. Bank Shopper Cash Rewards® Visa Signature® Card
practical_advice: Closed to new applicants as of June 2026. Existing cardholders keep the 6%/3% structure, but you need roughly $1,600+ a year at your two 6% retailers to break even on the $95 fee. Shopping today? The no-fee Cash+ covers similar ground.

name: U.S. Bank Cash+® Visa Signature® Card
practical_advice: Cash+ is great if you're willing to set (and reset) categories. Two 5% picks per quarter can be powerful, and the 2% lane covers a daily spend area.

name: United Gateway℠ Credit Card
features: 2 free checked bags after $10K annual spend
practical_advice: The no-annual-fee way to earn United miles on everyday spending. Bags aren't free out of the gate—you need $10,000 in a calendar year to unlock two checked bags—so treat it as an earn card first.

name: Bank of America® Premium Rewards® Credit Card
practical_advice: A simple travel card that pays for itself: 2x travel and dining, 1.5x everywhere else, and two credits that erase the $95 fee if you fly even once a year. Best if you bank with BofA—after the May 2026 overhaul most people top out at a 50% boost. No transfer partners or lounges.

name: Bank of America® Premium Rewards® Elite
practical_advice: Worth it only if you actually use the credits and lounges: $300 airline + $150 lifestyle erases most of the $550 fee, and four Priority Pass Select memberships is unusually generous for a household. Airfare redemptions get a 20% discount (≈1.2¢/point). If you barely fly, simpler cards win.

name: Bank of America® Travel Rewards® Credit Card
practical_advice: No-fee travel points without homework: 1.5x everything, 3x through the portal, redeemed at a clean 1¢ toward travel or dining. The BofA Rewards boost is what makes it punch above its weight—but after the May 2026 overhaul, the 75% tier takes $1M in balances. Look elsewhere for lounges or credits.

name: Choice Privileges® Select Mastercard®
practical_advice: The 30,000 anniversary points cover the $95 fee on their own, so if you stay with Choice even occasionally this is a painless keeper you don't have to babysit.

name: Bilt Obsidian Card
features: Up to 1.25x rent & mortgage, no fee
practical_advice: The closest replacement for the old Bilt Mastercard: pick 3x on dining or groceries for the year, and the $100 hotel credit covers the $95 fee with two Bilt Travel stays. Housing rewards are a bonus, not the reason to carry it.

name: Bilt Palladium Card
practical_advice: Really a travel card that happens to do housing: the $400 hotel credit plus $200 Bilt Cash each January beat the $495 fee before Priority Pass or points. Skip it if you book hotels direct or take one-night trips—and there's no Global Entry credit.
